findings.title: Design fully implements the slice plan entry within architectural bounds
findings.description: Every element of slice plan entry 129 maps to a design decision: port to `openai_codex` with bundled-binary-first/PATH fallback (D2), `codex = ["openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1"]` extra replacing the stale pyproject GitHub-install comment (D1, matches the current `pyproject.toml` comment), effort via `ReasoningEffort` closing #171 with `applies_effort=True` (D5), per-turn usage mapped to `TokenUsage`/`RunTelemetry` (D6), the missing-extra error + doctor row + model-list marker + README (Part B), and `sq auth login --device-code` / `logout` / `status` with account email/plan (Part C). The architecture's multi-provider requirements (register at import, self-contained credential resolution, no core-engine changes) are respected: no squadron token store is added, `~/.codex/auth.json` remains the Codex runtime's store, and all new machinery lives in the provider/CLI layers. The `InteractiveLogin` addition is correctly characterized as an additive optional capability relative to the Authentication Patterns section, with a documented trigger for updating that section if a second provider adopts it. Anti-pattern cleanup from slice 128 is preserved: capability dispatch via `isinstance` rather than profile-name or auth-type string checks, and D8 removes the silent `final_response or ""` fallback in favor of an explicit `ProviderError`, consistent with AGENTS.md's no-silent-fallback rule.

findings.title: `sq model list` marker path does not specify handling for aliases whose profile or provider cannot be resolved
findings.description: D9 states that `sq model list` "resolves each alias's profile through `ensure_provider_loaded` + `get_provider` and tests `isinstance(provider, ExtraRequirement)`". Both lookups can raise for inputs outside this slice's control: user aliases in `~/.config/squadron/models.toml` may reference a profile name that does not exist (`get_profile` raises `KeyError`), and user profiles in `providers.toml` may declare a provider type with no registered implementation (`ensure_provider_loaded` swallows the import failure silently by design, then `get_provider` raises `KeyError`). Today's `sq model list` (`src/squadron/cli/commands/models.py`) never touches the provider layer, so this design introduces a new per-alias failure path into a command that currently cannot fail on user alias config. The design's own integration requirement — "`sq doctor` and `sq model list` run cleanly with and without the extra" — and the no-regression posture ("Other profiles' `sq auth login` behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged") leave this case unmet unless the design states the degradation: an alias whose profile or provider cannot be resolved simply gets no marker (treated as if the provider does not implement `ExtraRequirement`), never a crash. Add that one sentence to D9 or the model-list bullet in "Sub-part B surfaces".

findings.title: Deferred slice 907's empty `[codex]` extra premise is superseded by this design
findings.description: Slice 907 (status: deferred) designed the `[codex]` extra as intentionally empty — "PyPI rejects direct URL references" — with the extra existing only as a documentation target. This slice populates the extra with a real PyPI dependency (`openai-codex`), which removes 907's stated reason for emptiness. D1 notes it "replaces the stale pyproject comment", which is the right call, but if 907 is ever revived its codex-extra section must not reintroduce the empty extra on top of this slice's declaration. No action required for this design; worth a one-line note in 907 or the slice plan when either is next touched.
